key_insight: In older adults in Kinshasa, neuropsychiatric symptoms showed distinct plasma protein associations, with NEFL providing the strongest signal linking symptom burden to neuroaxonal injury.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform dementia biomarker research in underrepresented African populations, but do not establish diagnostic or treatment utility.
method: Cross-sectional EVCD-RDC analysis: 779 of 1,044 participants had plasma proteomic data.
Assessed symptoms using NPI and GDS and measured proteins with the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120.
Used adjusted regression, exploratory factor analysis, and false-discovery-rate correction.
evidence_signal: NEFL was associated with overall NPI burden and the behavioural/motor dimension (both FDR<0.001); IL-6 and CCL13 correlated with depression scores, and APOE protein with nighttime behaviour.
watch_item: This is observational dementia research—not AI cancer drug discovery—and its cross-sectional associations require longitudinal replication before causal or clinical interpretation.
paper_title: Neuropsychiatric symptom clusters and plasma proteomic signatures across cognitive ageing and dementia in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional analysis of the EVCD-RDC cohort
